title: Multi-Region Capacity Handshake — Retrospective and Action Items
body:
Meeting: Multi-Region Capacity Handshake (weekly sync)
Date: 2026-03-14
Owner / note-taker: Aisha Patel
Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Diego, Priya, Samir, Helena (SRE), Jay (Serving Runtime)

Purpose
- Sync on short-term capacity moves and region handoffs for next 7 days.
- Review prewarming and warm-pool effectiveness from last weekend incident.
- Align on temporary routing policies and mitigation play for unexpected regional surges.

Quick TL;DR
- Weekend: unexpected burst in APAC-East (VK region) caused ~18% increase in queued requests for ~90m. Warm pool in that region mitigated tail latencies, but cold-start tokens increased costs by ~12% for affected customers.
- Decision: expand warm-pool prewarming window in APAC-East from 30m to 90m for peak hours (09:00–22:00 local), pilot through 2026-03-22.
- Action: implement autoscaler hysteresis tweak + a cross-region soft-drain policy to allow graceful eviction before fallback routing. Owner: Marco. ETA: 2026-03-18.

Metrics snapshot (observed)
- Peak queued requests (APAC-East): 42k requests/min at 2026-03-13 16:20 UTC.
- Median service token latency during event: +34ms over baseline; P95 spiked by 270ms (baseline P95 ~ 180ms).
- Warm-pool hit rate pre-event: 87%; during event: 73%.
- Cost delta (event window): +12% GPU-hours due to additional preemption/restarts.

Root cause hypothesis (short)
- Secondary scheduling delays from a node eviction storm in the regional cluster triggered degraded placement throughput. Evictions were correlated with an autoscaler race condition when spot reclaim signals arrived while scale-up decisions were in-flight.
- Warm-pool capacity was sized for the 95th traffic profile measured over trailing 14 days — the burst fell outside that window due to an external partner campaign that was not signaled via event-bus.

What worked
- Warm-pool prevented a full cold-start cascade. Without it, P95 would likely have exceeded 500ms and higher error rates.
- Cross-region fallback routing kept higher-priority customers (tier: enterprise-dedicated) within SLA by rerouting to us-west-2 during the tail of the incident.

What to improve
1) Telemetry gaps: no clear labeling on warm-pool fills by PR pipeline / rollout ID. Need to attribute warm-pool usage to campaigns/rollouts. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2026-03-21.
2) Autoscaler race: Introduce a short distributed lock or leader epoch check before applying scale-down when spot reclaim signals are present. Owner: Marco + Jay. ETA: 2026-03-18.
3) Prewarming policy: make warm-pool window adaptive to traffic velocity signals and publisher webhooks (if partner triggers detected). Owner: Priya + Diego. ETA: Pilot by 2026-03-22.
4) Cost signal: add a daily delta alert for GPU-hours vs rolling baseline per region; threshold 8% sustained to trigger finance ops review. Owner: Samir. ETA: 2026-03-19.

Action items (concrete)
- MARCO: Implement autoscaler hysteresis + soft-drain hook to postpone immediate evictions for nodes with active model KV caches. Add unit tests for leader-epoch gating. (2026-03-18)
- PRIYA: Instrument warm-pool fills with rollout_id and campaign_tag; emit metric warm.pool.fill.source. Add dashboard panel. (2026-03-21)
- DIEGO: Wire partner event-bus subscriber into prewarm controller; if partner campaign tag present, increase warm capacity by +25% for window. (Pilot 2026-03-22)
- SAMIR: Create daily cost-delta alert and runback script that reconciles GPU-hour anomalies to billing for the 7-day window. (2026-03-19)
- HELENA: Run SRE runbook drill for cross-region failover; validate runbook steps 1–7 and time-to-failover target < 3m. (2026-03-20)
- JAY: Assess model placement bottlenecks (kv-cache warmup latency) and propose a fast-path prefetch for top-10 models by traffic. (2026-03-25)

Risks and trade-offs discussed
- Increasing warm-pool windows increases regional baseline GPU-hours -> higher steady-state cost. Trade-off accepted temporarily for availability during the pilot. Finance will monitor.
- Aggressive soft-drain reduces eviction churn but may temporarily throttle scaling-in, which could increase costs. Need to calibrate thresholds.
- Cross-region fallback can mask root causes; ensure fallback is visible in post-incident dashboards so teams still fix primary region issues.

Follow-up items (questions left open)
- How to safely surface partner campaign signals into infra without overfitting (noise vs signal)? (Priya + Diego to prototype)
- Should we add a per-tenant warm-pool budget for customers on Dedicated plans to guarantee SLA? (Product + Infra sync required)
- Do we need a region-level cold-start SLA (quantified)? Proposed: P95 cold-start < 800ms for hosted tier. (Discuss in product meeting 2026-03-17)

Notes / raw observations from logs (snippets)
- 2026-03-13T16:19Z: nodeevict: reason=spot-reclaim, reclaim_score=0.78, concurrent_scale_ops=3
- 2026-03-13T16:21Z: prewarm: fill_count=18, candidate_pool=4, fallback_routed=12 to us-west-2
- Slack thread: #infra-incidents thread id C01234ABCDE contains live debugging notes and handoffs.

Meeting decisions (explicit)
- Pilot extended warm-pool window in APAC-East for next 8 days during local peak hours. (agreed)
- Autoscaler change to include leader epoch check before applying scale-down during spot events. (agreed)
- Instrumentation requirement for attributing warm-pool usage to campaign/rollout IDs. (agreed)

Next sync
- Quick standup on 2026-03-18 to validate Marco's autoscaler change in staging and confirm no regressions.
- Full capacity review on 2026-03-22 to decide whether to extend/scale the pilot.

Appendix: quick checklist for on-call when region surge detected
- Verify warm-pool utilization & increase window if below 80% (console toggle)
- Check autoscaler logs for concurrent scale ops > 2 (if yes, engage infra lead)
- Trigger cross-region soft-fallback for tiered customers (only after 5m sustained queue growth)
- Notify product & partner ops if partner tag detected on spike

Notes to self (Aisha)
- Add this doc as an interim incident collateral in Confluence (link to be created after PR merges).
- Keep language lightweight — this is an operations handshake record, not a full postmortem.
